compiled_state.description:
Discovered by the plan-review gate while re-reviewing mirror F3 (contiguous-industrial-dugong), which consolidated the claim-time plan-review exemption into rebar.types.PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES.

## Problem

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:108 carries a hardcoded tuple:

    if pctx.ticket_type in ("session_log", "code_review", "identity"):

It short-circuits those types to a bare exempt PASS with no review run. The module imports nothing from rebar.types — verified by grep, no EXEMPT reference at all — so this is a seventh spelling list of the ticket-type vocabulary that nothing pins.

## Why F3 did not cover it, and why this is still a mirror

It is NOT a duplicate of PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES. That set is {bug, session_log, code_review, identity}; this one is the same set MINUS bug, because a bug no longer short-circuits — since epic 6982/R4 it gets a LIGHT ADVISORY review (DET floor + necessity probe). So the two answer different questions: "is this type exempt from the claim gate?" versus "does this type skip review entirely?". F3 correctly consolidated the first and left the second alone.

It is still a mirror worth closing: the three spellings must be TicketType members and nothing enforces it, so renaming code_review silently turns its short-circuit off and the type would start getting a full review with nothing failing — the same failure shape as the other mirrors in this epic.

## Approach — derive the subset

Name the bare-exempt set in rebar.types, derived from PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES rather than re-listed (it is the exempt set minus the types that take the bug review tier), and have workflow_ops consume it. Deriving is what keeps the two sets from drifting apart independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: workflow_ops.py:108 consumes a derived constant; no ticket-type spelling remains in that module. Verified by a test and by grep for the literals.
- [ ] AC2: membership is UNCHANGED — exactly session_log, code_review and identity short-circuit, and a bug still takes the light advisory tier rather than a bare exempt PASS. Verified by a test pinning both.
- [ ] AC3: every member of the derived set is a TicketType member. Verified by a test asserting the subset relation against get_args(TicketType).
- [ ] AC4: the derived set stays consistent with PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES. Verified by a test asserting the intended relation between them, so adding an exempt type forces a decision about the short-circuit rather than silently diverging.

## Testing

- python -m pytest tests/unit -k "plan_review or workflow_ops or exempt" -q — AC1-AC4.
- make lint && make typecheck.
